events.description: Ustinov orally orders General Staff to prepare a paratroop division, five military-transport aviation divisions, and readiness of two motorized rifle divisions in Turkestan MD.
Narrow group (Brezhnev, Suslov, Andropov, Ustinov, Gromyko) makes final decision to send Soviet troops into Afghanistan.
Ustinov announces decision to Defense Ministry leadership; directive signed to send contingents into DRA.
American military ships stationed in the Persian Gulf; reports of a possible US invasion of Iran influenced Ustinov.

Ustinov orally ordered the General Staff to prepare one paratroop division, five military-transport aviation divisions, raise readiness of two motorized rifle divisions in Turkestan MD, and fill a pontoon regiment.
Narrow group of leaders made the final political decision to send Soviet troops to Afghanistan.
Ustinov convened the Defense Ministry leadership, announced the decision, and a directive was prepared.
First printed directive signed by the Defense Minister ordering troops into the DRA.

sources_cited: Georgy M. Kornienko, The Cold War: Testimony of a Participant (Moscow, 1994)
Handwritten Resolution of the Politburo (prepared after the fact)
key_claims: Gromyko and Kornienko agreed March–October 1979 that sending troops would be impermissible.
Kornienko believes Ustinov was first to favor intervention, spurred by US naval deployments in the Persian Gulf and fears of an invasion of Iran.
Andropov was a hostage of KGB apparatus that portrayed Amin as an American agent and overstated Soviet capabilities.
General Staff leaders Ogarkov, Akhromeev and Varennikov opposed intervention on professional grounds, citing Vietnam, but were overruled.
The final decision was taken on 12 Dec 1979 by Brezhnev, Suslov, Andropov, Ustinov and Gromyko, not the full Politburo.
A Politburo resolution was signed after the fact by almost all members.
